::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Line with arrowhead in PGFPLOT](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/8007/line-with-arrowhead-in-pgfplot), asked by [Pie86](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/2731/pie86) on TeX Stack Exchange (2010-12-30; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> How can I add a line ending with an arrowhead in pgfplot?
>
> ```latex
> \begin{tikzpicture}
> \begin{axis}[grid=major,axis x line=middle,
>              axis y line=middle]
>
> \addplot[domain=0:1, no markers] {(x^2)*(3-2*x)};
>
> \addplot[] coordinates
>            {(0,0) (0.5,0)};
>
> \end{axis}
> \end{tikzpicture}
> ```
>
> I want the above line to end with an arrow but I can't figure out what to put in the brackets. Probably that's a dumb question but neither google nor the manual helped me:(
:::

Try the `after end axis` key.  It allows you to add arbitrary TikZ code and still access the plot's coordinate system.  It's documented in section 4.23 ("Miscellaneous Options") of the pgfplots 1.4 manual.

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usepackage{pgfplots}
\begin{document}
\begin{tikzpicture}
\begin{axis}[grid=major,axis x line=middle,
             axis y line=middle,
             after end axis/.code={
               \draw[red,->] (axis cs:0,0) -- (axis cs:0.5,0);
             }]
\addplot[domain=0:1, no markers] {(x^2)*(3-2*x)};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{document}
```
